title: Live/streaming replies in chat
contract: Three generations of it: edit-based streaming with saturated-preview dedup and oversized-edit splitting into continuation messages (platform-telegram.edit-message/.overflow-dedup/.overflow-split), native drafts (`sendMessageDraft`, Rich draft frames), and platform-native streaming APIs — Slack `chat.startStream`/`appendStream`/`stopStream` where the streamed message *is* the final message, with a one-shot capability latch and fallback to edit-based (platforms-a.slack-native-streaming); WeCom `msgtype: stream`; DingTalk AI Cards. title: Regional and enterprise-chat breadth (DingTalk, Feishu/Lark, WeCom, WeCom Callback, Yuanbao)
contract: Five adapters, ~60 entries: DingTalk Stream Mode with AI Cards and emoji reactions; Feishu with a 3-tier group-rules admission policy, webhook mode with signature and anomaly tracking, interactive approval cards, **document-comment intelligent reply** with its own access-control CLI, meeting-invitation events, and six agent-facing doc/drive tools; WeCom with native `msgtype: stream`, a per-chat send queue with a token bucket, and a separate Callback adapter with WXBizMsgCrypt; Yuanbao with a reverse-engineered wire protocol, SignManager auth, COS media upload, stickers, and five agent tools.
governance: Each would add a new egress domain family and a new inbound door — the surface-area cost is the argument, not the effort.
historical_exclusion_reason: Wrong audience for this product. These are corporate-suite chat platforms for a market Nerva does not serve, and each one is not a thin adapter but a vendor SDK plus a crypto/callback surface plus a tool family — Feishu alone is six agent-facing tools that read and write a document store. Bringing them in would roughly double the channel-layer surface area and the egress allowlist for capability the owner will never exercise, on a product whose thesis is a small, auditable, local-first system. The transferable ideas are already claimed by other rows: WeCom's per-chat token bucket belongs in the send limiter, Feishu's approval cards in the approvals row, DingTalk's reaction lifecycle in the feedback row. Re-open only on a signed design partner in that market, and then one platform at a time behind its own flag.
